newsitem.title: PANAMA: Panama's Kuna Indians sell handicrafts in cyberspace.
newsitem.headline: Panama's Kuna Indians sell handicrafts in cyberspace.

text.p: Panama's traditional Kuna Indians have entered cyberspace and the Central American nation's trademark handicraft can now be purchased on the Internet.

Now you don't have to fly to Panama to own a "mola," the Kunas' centuries-old tradition of hand-sewn cloths worn as blouses by women. The fabrics, depicting traditional Kuna images of animals and geometric shapes, are available at prices of up to $50 on the web site (http://www.peoplink.org./).
Set up by a non-profit organisation based in the U.S. state of Maryland, the web site shows a picture of a Kuna woman wearing a mola and 20 illustrations of molas available for purchase.
Proceeds benefit a Panamanian coooperative that works with 1,500 Kuna women who stitch the molas by hand.
